evidence: The premise checks out: horizon/verify-instrument.sh asserted only directory existence for the memento skills, so gutting them to stubs left a verifier that passes on a dead instrument. PR #44 (merged 2026-09-04, 'Fixes promptctl-horizon-y9g') repeats the same diagnosis in its own words - 'the verifier went green on a broken instrument' - so the finding was true and the deferral to that ticket was actually honoured three days later.
guidance_note: Before deleting an implementation, grep the repo for every consumer that provisions from or asserts on it, and in the same PR either repoint it or tighten its assertion to fail loudly, rather than leaving a green check on a dependency you just killed.

evidence: I fetched promptctl/memento's .claude-plugin/marketplace.json at commit 6711491 (its state when this PR merged): it declares "name": "memento", so the documented `/plugin install memento@memento` alias resolves. The reviewer's general principle is right and it self-labelled the claim unverified; the agent had already verified it by running the install against an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so the pushback was correct on the facts.
guidance_note: When a doc's copy-paste command depends on a fact held in another repo, state the verified fact (here: that marketplace's declared `name`) beside the command or in the PR body, so a reader and a reviewer without cross-repo access can check it instead of guessing.

evidence: promptctl/memento's marketplace.json at merge time (commit 6711491) declares two plugins, `memento` and `auto-bottle`, and auto-bottle--v0.1.0 is a real tag - so the name the reviewer suspected was invented is real. The law citation is apt rather than decorative: the reviewer's proposed remedy was to restate the other repo's plugin roster in this repo's manifests, which is literally a second copy of a fact this repo does not own.
guidance_note: Put the cross-repo verification you already ran - the exact commands and their output - into the PR body when a file asserts another repo's contents, so a claim the reviewer structurally cannot check arrives already evidenced instead of costing a thread.

evidence: horizon/GOAL_PROMPT.md is untouched by this diff and still directs an autonomous agent to memento's in-repo pickup and close-out logic, which this PR replaced with install pointers - the reviewer was right and even right to hedge on whether horizon is live. PR #44's body confirms the agent's stated reason for deferring ('Fixing the pin source alone would not have fixed the loop'; `next` had moved into the lit binary, not into promptctl/memento), so this genuinely was a cross-repo pinning design rather than a wording edit.
guidance_note: An extraction PR should grep the repo for every mention of the moved names and list each hit's disposition (repointed here / tracked as X) in the PR body, so the reviewer is not the one discovering the in-repo consumers.

evidence: The reviewer aimed at the wrong artifact (keywords, when the description already says pointers-only) but was right that the manifest advertises capability the plugin no longer has. The agent's justification - stubs 'deliberately retain their original trigger phrases' so seekers find them - is exactly the defect PR #45 had to undo on 2026-09-04: the stub plugin kept the name `memento` and the three skill names, won the `memento:*` namespace over the installed real plugin, and a session invoking address-pr-reviews got the pointer while the real 298-line procedure sat loaded; #45 deleted the stub plugin and moved the redirect to the README.
guidance_note: A stub that keeps the real component's name, trigger phrases and manifest facets is a second declaration of that capability, not documentation - put the redirect where readers look for repo facts (README) and never ship a runtime component whose only content is a forwarding address.

narrative: One review round, five findings, on a single-commit extraction that moved three memento skills to promptctl/memento and left pointer stubs. Two findings (F1, F4) correctly identified that the in-repo horizon harness still provisions and describes the deleted implementations; the agent accepted both, filed promptctl-horizon-y9g, merged 19 minutes after opening with the review dismissed, and the ticket was genuinely closed by #44 three days later. Two (F2, F3) were the reviewer unable to see the destination repo, and the agent's pushbacks were correct on facts I re-verified against promptctl/memento's marketplace.json at merge time. The one bad call is F5: the agent defended the stub's retained trigger phrases as the design, and that design is what PR #45 deleted on 2026-09-04 after the stubs shadowed the installed plugin's skills in a live session. No finding here was caused by an earlier fix in this PR - there is one commit and one round.
guidance_observations: Two of five findings existed only because the reviewer could not see the destination repo, and the agent had already run the verifying installs before opening the PR - the evidence just was not in the PR body where it would have pre-empted the threads.

The PR merged with an accepted S4 and an accepted S3 unfixed and the review dismissed; the ticket was real and honoured, but nothing in the PR made the now-dead horizon dependency fail loudly in the three days before #44 landed.

The reviewer probed the stub's manifest facets (F5) but never the skill-name namespace collision that actually broke a session, and the agent's own pre-merge checks did not either - neither side has a 'does this name already exist in an installed plugin' check.
